drug_class: Alkylating agent / RNA polymerase II inhibitor (cancer chemotherapy)
purpose: Lurbinectedin is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat adults with a type of lung cancer called small cell lung cancer (SCLC) that has spread or come back after previous treatment. It is given when at least one other chemotherapy has already been tried. Your doctor may choose this medicine when other options have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: This medicine works by getting inside cancer cells and attaching to their DNA, which is like the cell's instruction manual. By doing this, it blocks a key protein that cancer cells need to copy themselves and grow. Without being able to follow their instructions, the cancer cells are unable to multiply and eventually die off.
common_side_effects: Fatigue or feeling very tired, nausea, decreased appetite, low blood cell counts (which can make you more prone to infections, bruising, or feeling weak), constipation, shortness of breath, and muscle or joint aches. Your blood will be checked regularly to watch for these issues.
warnings: This medicine can cause seriously low blood counts, which raises your risk of dangerous infections, bleeding, or severe anemia — tell your doctor right away if you have a fever, chills, unusual bruising, or bleeding. It can also cause liver problems, so your liver will be monitored. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as this medicine can harm an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control during and for a period after treatment. Tell your care team about all other medicines you take, as some can interact with this drug.
typical_dosing: Lurbinectedin is given through an IV (into a vein) in a cancer clinic or infusion center, typically once every 3 weeks. Each infusion takes about 60 minutes. Your doctor will decide the exact dose based on your body size and overall health, and may adjust it if you have side effects.
